summary: Today’s pulse tracks Children among dead at Algeria foster care home blaze - president, Protests in Ukrainian cities against Zelensky's removal of defence minister, and Outrage at sacking of Ukraine’s defence minister overshadows Starmer’s final visit as PM – Europe live. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are burnham, climate, and england. In the background, Making Mahmood chancellor shows Burnham ‘subservient to City’, claims Polanski – UK politics live and Trump to meet Darline Graham at the White House today – US politics live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Children among dead at Algeria foster care home blaze - president
headlines.description: Eleven people have died and 19 other have suffered injuries in the overnight blaze, the authorities say.

headlines.title: Protests in Ukrainian cities against Zelensky's removal of defence minister
headlines.description: Ukraine's president has not explained Mykhailo Fedorov's dismissal, which is causing great upset among civil society and the military.

headlines.title: Outrage at sacking of Ukraine’s defence minister overshadows Starmer’s final visit as PM – Europe live
headlines.description: Protests in Lviv and Kyiv as Zelenskyy faces anger after removing the popular Mykhailo Fedorov in Madrid Meanwhile, the EU’s top court has ruled that a controversial Spanish law that offered an amnesty to those who planned and participated in the failed and illegal push for Catalan independence does not violate the bloc’s rules.

headlines.title: Making Mahmood chancellor shows Burnham ‘subservient to City’, claims Polanski – UK politics live
headlines.description: Green leader says expected appointment shows new PM ‘won’t challenge the power of the bankers, or tax their wealth’ Couples could legally marry in forests, on beaches, at sea or in their gardens under new proposals, the Press Association reports. PA says a government consultation announced today , covering rules in England and Wales, could help cut the costs of weddings and mean two ceremonies are no longer required to cover different faiths. PA says: The average wedding in England is estimated to cost more than £20,000, with venue hire alone typically accounting for around £6,000 without catering. The system as it stands means some couples have two ceremonies – one where they feel their beliefs are best reflected and another making their marriage legal.

headlines.title: Trump to meet Darline Graham at the White House today – US politics live
headlines.description: President will meet new Republican senator who has taken over the seat following the death of her brother Lindsey Graham It’s a reminder to consumers and truckers of the costs of the Iran war and the unpredictable rhetoric from both Washington and Tehran. A year ago today, the AAA says, the average price for a gallon of diesel was $3.72, almost a dollar and a quarter less than it is now.

headlines.title: How green is Andy Burnham? Britain’s next PM faces tough climate decisions
headlines.description: Heatwaves, high energy prices, calls for reindustrialisation and North Sea drilling are all high on the to-do list UK politics live – latest updates Wildfires cast a pall of smoke this week over Greater Manchester , whose former mayor Andy Burnham stands on the threshold of No 10. Amid three UK heatwaves so far this year, which have killed thousands of people in England and Wales, damaged harvests and left children crying in classrooms , the new prime minister’s plans for the climate crisis remain as shrouded as his city. “Burnham has been very quiet about the climate [crisis] so far,” says Chris Venables, an environmental campaigner and fellow at the Green Alliance thinktank. “I don’t think [it] is at the forefront of his mind, but that does not mean he will water down this agenda.”

headlinePool.title: Trump’s Board of Peace drops full Gaza recovery plan in favour of tiny pilot scheme
headlinePool.description: Revised plan aims to ‘keep something going’ amid fears Netanyahu may gamble on new all-out offensive before Israeli elections The Gaza recovery plan being pursued by Donald Trump’s Board of Peace (BoP) has shrunk dramatically from an ambitious blueprint for the reconstruction of the whole territory to a small pilot project in the south of the strip. Even the envisaged pilot scheme – involving a temporary camp for a tiny fraction of Gaza’s 2 million displaced people, with a Palestinian administration, police and a small international security force – is not expected to take shape before the end of the year.

headlinePool.title: More than 800 Canadian wildfires burning as air quality alerts extend to US
headlinePool.description: The air quality in large parts of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by authorities.

headlinePool.title: Italian officials handed jail terms for Genoa bridge disaster that killed 43
headlinePool.description: The ex-head of Italy's motorway operator Giovanni Castellucci was handed a 12-year term over the 2018 bridge collapse.

headlinePool.title: Hal Williams, actor best known for Sanford and Son and 227, dies aged 91
headlinePool.description: The actor, who also appeared in The Waltons and Private Benjamin, died at his home in California Hal Williams, the actor best known for TV roles in Sanford & Son and 227, has died at the age of 91. His representative confirmed that Williams died on 15 July at his home in California .

headlinePool.title: Offer teenagers a meningitis B vaccine on NHS, advisers tell UK government
headlinePool.description: JCVI says children should have one or two doses of menB vaccine at age 15, depending on if they had one as a baby Teenagers should be offered a vaccine on the NHS to protect against deadly meningitis B (menB), government advisers have recommended. The move by the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI), which needs approval from the government, means young people should get a jab around the age of 15, with catch-up programmes for those who would otherwise miss out.

headlinePool.title: UK government drops plan to stop paying coastguard volunteers
headlinePool.description: Move raises questions over position of the head of the Maritime and Coastguard Agency UK politics live – latest updates Ministers have U-turned on plans to strip volunteer coastguard officers of their hourly pay after intense criticism of the plan. The announcement, made by the maritime minister in parliament on Thursday, was described as a huge win for coastguards, many of whom had said they would reduce their hours or leave the service altogether if the government had pushed ahead. It has raised questions over the position of Virginia McVea, the head of the Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA).

headlinePool.title: Iran accuses US of ‘barbaric’ strike near hospital as Kuwait says it is under attack – Middle East crisis live
headlinePool.description: Foreign ministry spokesman says children’s cancer hospital had to be evacuated in Ahvaz; Kuwait says it responding to renewed Iranian drone attacks US attacks oil tanker in strait of Hormuz as strikes reported in Tehran The Lebanese foreign minister, Youssef Raggi, said Lebanon has made a decision to “end Hezbollah’s military presence” and that decisions on war and foreign policy are the “exclusive prerogative of the Lebanese state”. The Lebanese government is pushing to disarm Hezbollah, one of the most heavily armed militias in the Middle East, and it has become a central component of the US-brokered talks between Lebanon and Israel. Lebanon has made its choice: there will be no return to dual authority, and there is no longer any place for weapons outside the authority of the state or for decisions taken outside its constitutional institutions. The decision to end Hezbollah’s military presence is a sovereign Lebanese decision. It preceded the Framework Agreement and paved the way for it, affirming that decisions on war and peace, as well as foreign policy, are now the exclusive prerogative of the Lebanese state.”

headlinePool.title: Hong Kong official warns booksellers on security risks after raids
headlinePool.description: The police operation marks the third round of arrests targeting independent bookstores in four months.

headlinePool.title: MI5 lied about relations with neo-Nazi informant, watchdog says
headlinePool.description: Review of case criticises handling of agent X, who exploited role with agency to violently threaten his girlfriend MI5 has been reprimanded by a watchdog for lying about its relationship with a neo-Nazi informant, who had exploited his role with the spy agency to violently threaten his girlfriend. The Investigatory Powers Commissioner’s Office (Ipco) criticised MI5’s handling of a man known only as agent X, and said some of its officers had initially misled the courts and the regulator about his true status.
